creature_description: An immense legendary cephalopod with a bulbous mantle and eight muscular arms, each lined from base to tip with visible circular suckers.
amazing_fact: Sailors once described it as large enough to be mistaken for an island.

creature_description: A soft-bodied marine animal with eight flexible arms, two rows of suckers along each arm, and skin that can change color and texture.
amazing_fact: It has three hearts and blue blood.

creature_description: A pale deep-sea octopus with eight short arms, full-length suckers, and two ear-like fins above its eyes.
amazing_fact: It lives at some of the greatest known ocean depths.

creature_description: A delicate pelagic octopus whose female carries a thin paper-like eggcase and has eight sucker-bearing arms.
amazing_fact: Despite its name, it is an octopus rather than a true nautilus.

creature_description: A small octopus with eight sucker-lined arms and bright blue warning rings that flash across yellow-brown skin.
amazing_fact: Its venom can be dangerous despite its tiny size.

creature_description: A long-armed octopus with full-length suckers that can flatten, stripe, and reshape itself to imitate other animals.
amazing_fact: It can imitate creatures such as sea snakes and flatfish.

creature_description: A large reddish octopus with eight thick sucker-covered arms and a broad mantle.
amazing_fact: It is among the largest octopus species by mass.

creature_description: A small octopus with eight sucker-lined arms, often seen walking across sand with a compact mantle.
amazing_fact: It can carry shells as portable shelter.

creature_description: A nearly transparent octopus with eight delicate arms and faintly visible internal organs.
amazing_fact: Its transparency helps it disappear in open water.

creature_description: A pelagic octopus with eight arms; females carry a flowing web between some arms.
amazing_fact: Females can be vastly larger than males.

creature_description: A long-bodied cephalopod with eight arms plus two exceptionally long feeding tentacles with terminal sucker clubs.
amazing_fact: Its eyes are among the largest in the animal kingdom.

creature_description: A heavy deep-sea squid with eight arms and two feeding tentacles armed with hooks and suckers.
amazing_fact: It is known for rotating hooks on its tentacles.

creature_description: A flattened cephalopod with eight arms and two retractable feeding tentacles, surrounded by a finned mantle.
amazing_fact: It can rapidly change skin patterns for camouflage.

creature_description: A small rounded squid with eight arms, two longer tentacles, and a short compact body.
amazing_fact: Some species glow through a partnership with luminous bacteria.

creature_description: A dark red, webbed cephalopod with eight arms lined by soft spines rather than ordinary suckers.
amazing_fact: It turns its webbed arms inside out as a defensive display.

creature_description: A shelled cephalopod with dozens of slender cirri around the mouth instead of eight arms.
amazing_fact: Its chambered shell regulates buoyancy.

creature_description: A small deep-water squid with a coiled internal shell and ten limbs.
amazing_fact: Its shell resembles a tiny ram's horn.

creature_description: A fictional squid-like creature with ten limbs and a segmented shell-shaped mantle.
amazing_fact: Its mantle chambers are said to amplify distant sounds.

creature_description: A jellyfish with a broad bell and an enormous curtain of trailing stinging tentacles.
amazing_fact: It can have hundreds or thousands of tentacles.

creature_description: A translucent jellyfish with a round bell, four visible gonads, and many fine marginal tentacles.
amazing_fact: Its bell often shows four horseshoe-shaped rings.

creature_description: A cube-shaped jellyfish with clusters of tentacles hanging from its four lower corners.
amazing_fact: It has remarkably complex eyes for a jellyfish.

creature_description: A flower-like stationary animal with many short stinging tentacles arranged around a central mouth.
amazing_fact: Some species form long-lived partnerships with clownfish.

creature_description: A tiny freshwater polyp with a tubular body and a ring of stinging tentacles.
amazing_fact: It is famous for its ability to regenerate.

creature_description: A floating colonial organism with a blue gas-filled crest and very long stinging fishing threads.
amazing_fact: It is not a single jellyfish but a colony of specialized animals.

creature_description: An elongated leathery echinoderm with branching feeding tentacles around its mouth.
amazing_fact: Some can eject internal organs to distract predators.

creature_description: A starfish with numerous arms radiating from a central disk and tube feet on the underside.
amazing_fact: Some sun stars can have more than twenty arms.

creature_description: A crinoid with many feathery arms used to catch drifting food particles.
amazing_fact: It can crawl and sometimes swim using its arms.

creature_description: A disk-shaped echinoderm with five long, thin, sharply flexible arms.
amazing_fact: It moves mainly by rowing its arms rather than using tube feet.

creature_description: A brightly colored sea slug with a soft elongated body and external gills or feathery projections.
amazing_fact: Some store stinging cells from prey for their own defense.

creature_description: A large soft sea slug with ear-like sensory flaps and a broad crawling foot.
amazing_fact: It can release purple ink-like fluid when threatened.

creature_description: A fictional transparent creature with a jellyfish bell and eight smooth octopus-like trailing limbs without suckers.
amazing_fact: It is said to glow only during new moons.

creature_description: A fictional squid-like animal with eight thin limbs and sucker pads restricted to the very tips.
amazing_fact: It is rumored to weave temporary silk-like feeding nets.

creature_description: A fictional rolling sphere covered in fifty short sucker-bearing appendages.
amazing_fact: It supposedly rolls downhill rather than swims.

creature_description: A fictional eel-shaped animal with eight short smooth limbs near its head and no suckers.
amazing_fact: Legends say it senses storms through its skin.

creature_description: A fictional translucent cephalopod with six arms covered in pale suction cups.
amazing_fact: Its body is said to fade almost completely in moonlight.

creature_description: A fictional rooted sea plant with twelve thick vines covered in sticky pads.
amazing_fact: Its vines supposedly close when whales pass overhead.

creature_description: A fictional bioluminescent squid with eight arms and two tentacles, all dotted with glowing suckers.
amazing_fact: Its pulses allegedly follow a rhythm every thirteen seconds.

creature_description: A fictional armored predator with nine uneven limbs and sucker clusters only at the tips.
amazing_fact: Old divers called it the lantern-eater.

creature_description: A fictional eight-armed mimic with smooth rubbery limbs and no suckers.
amazing_fact: Its silhouette is said to fool sailors during fog.

creature_description: A fictional jellyfish with a black bell and twelve ribbon-like glowing tentacles.
amazing_fact: It supposedly leaves a faint blue trail in cold water.

creature_description: A fictional reef-dwelling phantom with many branch-like arms and a mask-shaped head.
amazing_fact: It is said to appear only near abandoned reefs.

creature_description: A fictional giant eel with a serpentine body, four whisker-like feelers, and lamp-like eyes.
amazing_fact: Maps claim it follows underwater volcanic ridges.

creature_description: A mythic sea-dweller with human-like upper features, scaled lower body, and webbed hands.
amazing_fact: Irish folklore describes a magical cap that lets it travel through water.

creature_description: A mythic water spirit that usually appears as a powerful horse with dripping mane.
amazing_fact: Scottish tales warn travelers not to ride it.

creature_description: A mythic sea-horse creature with a horse's forebody and fish tail.
amazing_fact: It was often depicted drawing Poseidon's chariot.

creature_description: A mythic sea monster traditionally depicted with multiple snapping heads and writhing lower limbs.
amazing_fact: It was said to menace ships in a narrow strait.

creature_description: A mythic sea hazard personified as a monstrous whirlpool.
amazing_fact: The phrase between Scylla and Charybdis means facing two dangers.

creature_description: A mythic singer associated with dangerous shores and irresistible calls.
amazing_fact: In early Greek art, sirens were bird-like rather than fish-tailed.

creature_description: A mythic sea nymph often depicted with flowing hair and marine ornaments.
amazing_fact: Ancient stories describe them as attendants of the sea god Nereus.

creature_description: An extinct giant shark with a broad body, powerful tail, and rows of enormous teeth.
amazing_fact: Its name means big tooth.

creature_description: A legendary serpent-like marine creature with a long scaled body and finned crest.
amazing_fact: Reports of sea serpents may have been inspired by oarfish sightings.

creature_description: A fictional cosmic entity often depicted with an octopus-like head, facial tendrils, wings, and a colossal humanoid form.
amazing_fact: It originates in early twentieth-century cosmic-horror fiction.

creature_description: An Ainu legendary giant octopus-like sea being with enormous tentacles.
amazing_fact: It is traditionally associated with a bay in Hokkaido.

creature_description: A Japanese sea spirit often shown as a dark, bald humanoid rising from waves.
amazing_fact: Folklore says it can demand a barrel from sailors.

creature_description: A Japanese water dragon or serpent associated with rivers and deep pools.
amazing_fact: It appears in old chronicles as a powerful water spirit.

creature_description: A Mesopotamian primordial sea deity often interpreted in later retellings as a dragon-like chaos monster.
amazing_fact: Her name is connected with the salt sea in Babylonian myth.

creature_description: A Norse world serpent said to encircle the ocean surrounding Midgard.
amazing_fact: Myth says it will release its tail at Ragnarok.
